note: Ibrutinib went into B-cell lymphoma patients on probe-measured BTK occupancy in rodents and dogs and responses in pet dogs with lymphoma; occupancy, dose and response all held in MCL, while rat and dog toxicology missed thrombocytopenia and atrial fibrillation.
label: Mantle cell lymphoma (BTK inhibitors)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (ASH 2007 abstract, Blood 110:1592, and Honigberg 2010 PNAS); dog occupancy also in FDA pharmacology review.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the probe-occupancy system was published with the first-in-human trial already running (NCT00849654 posted 2009).
engagement.model: BTK active-site probe occupancy in mice, rats and dogs
engagement.note: Earliest public date: the ASH 2007 abstract showed probe-measured full BTK occupancy in mice before any human dosing; PNAS 2010 added dogs.
engagement.short: Probe occupancy in mice and dogs
engagement.quote: A single oral dose of PCI-32765 (10mg/kg) delivered to mice leads to rapid and complete inhibition of Btk in spleen.

engagement.magnitude_basis: complete BTK active-site occupancy in animals and in patients' PBMCs; doses not scaled between species
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year from Pollyea ASH 2009 abstract (doi:10.1182/blood.V114.22.3713.3713): "PD studies showed the average drug occupancy of Btk in patient PBMCs in this cohort was 89% at 4 hours post-dose". NCT00849654 has no posted results, so registry_date is null. Mouse occupancy was public in 2007, before the trial, so not a retrodiction.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Advani reports the human probe data and cites the animal work but does not set them side by side. Population is mixed B-cell malignancies including MCL; occupancy was not reported for MCL separately.
engagement.model: BTK active-site probe occupancy in mice, rats and dogs
engagement.note: Earliest public date: the ASH 2009 phase 1 abstract (Pollyea) reported 89% BTK occupancy in patient PBMCs on the same probe; Advani 2012 showed full occupancy at 2.5 mg/kg/day.
engagement.quote: Full occupancy of the BTK active site occurred at 2.5 mg/kg per day, and dose escalation continued to 12.5 mg/kg per day without reaching MTD.
engagement.reason: Patients reached full occupancy as in animals

dose.judgement: The stated model target is an occupancy target, not a mg/kg number; the trial design (escalate to three levels above full occupancy) shows it was used.
dose.model: BTK active-site probe occupancy in mice, rats and dogs
dose.note: Earliest public date: the ASH 2007 abstract set probe-measured full BTK occupancy in mice as the dosing readout carried into the phase 1 escalation.
dose.short: Full occupancy set as dose target
dose.quote: The Btk probe provides pharmacodynamic measurements that may allow optimization of dosing and schedule for in vivo studies and we are currently adapting the probe assays for use in monitoring the inhibition of Btk in human clinical trials.

dose.magnitude_basis: occupancy target (full active-site occupancy) reached at 2.5 mg/kg/day; MCL dose 560 mg is above it
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA clinical pharmacology review (NDA 205552) confirms >90% occupancy at 24 h at doses >=2.5 mg/kg and similar ORR from 2.5 to 12.5 mg/kg.
dose.judgement: margin_stated false: dogs tolerated 200 mg/kg with complete occupancy at 100 mg/kg, but that tolerability margin was in unpublished toxicology (public only in the 2013-14 FDA review), so I scored only the exposure half.
dose.model: BTK active-site probe occupancy in mice, rats and dogs
dose.note: Full occupancy was reached at 2.5 mg/kg/day with no MTD up to 12.5 mg/kg; the MCL dose (560 mg/day) sat above the occupancy dose.
dose.quote: Dose escalation proceeded until either the maximum-tolerated dose (MTD) was achieved or, in the absence of MTD, until three dose levels above full BTK occupancy by ibrutinib.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (ASH 2009 abstract online Nov 2009; first patient responses in a Pharmacyclics press release of 8 Dec 2009). Dog response count in Honigberg 2010 PNAS not read.
efficacy.judgement: Canine lymphoma is not MCL; it stands in as a cross-histology B-NHL model. Year proxy: dogs were treated before publication.
efficacy.model: Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
efficacy.note: Earliest public date: the ASH 2009 abstract reported ibrutinib activity in pet dogs with B-cell lymphoma before any human responses; PNAS 2010 detailed the responses.
efficacy.short: Responses in dogs with B-cell lymphoma
efficacy.quote: PCI-32765 is an oral, potent and selective covalent inhibitor of Btk which blocks BCR signaling and inhibits tumor growth in both mouse and spontaneous canine NHL models.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: objective response: dog responses (count not read) vs 68% ORR in R/R MCL
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year from the ASH 2011 interim abstract (doi:10.1182/blood.V118.21.442.442): "The objective response rate (ORR) by IWG criteria is 67% (16/24)". NCT01236391 results first posted 2015-03-13; NEJM online 2013-06-19.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. Direction only: dog lymphoma is DLBCL-like and ibrutinib did far less in human DLBCL, so the dog result says the class is active in B-NHL, not that MCL would respond best. Acalabrutinib in the same dogs is its own track (appended).
efficacy.model: Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
efficacy.note: Single-arm phase 2 PCYC-1104, primary endpoint ORR, no pre-set success bar: dogs predicted response and R/R MCL responded (67% ASH 2011 interim; 68% in 111 patients, NEJM 2013), so same.
efficacy.quote: A response rate of 68% (75 patients) was observed, with a complete response rate of 21% and a partial response rate of 47%; prior treatment with bortezomib had no effect on the response rate.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PDX drug response vs the source patient's response
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; how many MCL donor-PDX pairs were compared for ibrutinib was not read. A prospective PDX-guided pilot (NCT03219047) is registered; no results found.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the models were built from patients whose ibrutinib outcome was already known, so retro, not same; patient-level because it asks which patient responds.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived xenografts in human bone chips (MD Anderson)
efficacy.note: PDXs from 16 B-cell lymphoma patients, including MCL, reproduced their donors' drug responses, including primary and acquired ibrutinib resistance.
efficacy.quote: The PDXs maintained the same biological, histopathologic, and immunophenotypical features, retained similar genetic mutations, and produced comparable drug responses with the original patient tumors.

efficacy.population: MCL, relapsed/refractory and untreated (AVO trial, NCT04855695)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC12680032). Opening entry at the method's first MCL use (bioRxiv May 2025).
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo acalabrutinib-induced mass change in pretreatment MCL cells proposed as a per-patient sensitivity readout.
efficacy.short: Ex-vivo mass response as BTKi readout
efficacy.quote: In addition, changes in cell buoyant mass within primary patient specimens ex vivo correlate with sensitivity to Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in vivo in MCL and chronic lymphocytic leukemia, another B cell malignancy.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; the comparison is in the same paper.
efficacy.model: Ex-vivo single-cell buoyant-mass response (suspended microchannel resonator) of primary MCL cells to acalabrutinib

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo mass response (P<0.05) vs circulating-lymphocyte kinetics on 4 weeks of acalabrutinib
efficacy.population: MCL, relapsed/refractory and untreated (AVO trial, NCT04855695)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Four MCL patients (two more, two less sensitive), sensitivity defined by WBC kinetics, not the trial's primary endpoint; three of four untreated, outside the R/R population. One pirtobrutinib case is outside the member list.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: pre- and post-treatment samples were assayed together after the cycle-1 lymphocyte response was known, so retro, not same. Patient-level: it asks which patient responds.
efficacy.note: Pretreatment cells from the two acalabrutinib-sensitive patients lost mass ex vivo; the two less-sensitive patients' cells did not.
efficacy.quote: In addition, changes in cell buoyant mass within primary patient specimens ex vivo correlate with sensitivity to Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in vivo in MCL and chronic lymphocytic leukemia, another B cell malignancy.
efficacy.model: Ex-vivo single-cell buoyant-mass response (suspended microchannel resonator) of primary MCL cells to acalabrutinib

efficacy.population: MCL with TRAF2/BIRC3 lesions (15% of 165 patients)
efficacy.note: Cell lines with alternative NF-kB (TRAF2/BIRC3) lesions were ibrutinib-insensitive; predicts primary resistance in lesion-bearing patients.
efficacy.quote: Although they are associated with insensitivity to ibrutinib, lesions in the alternative NF-κB pathway conferred dependence on the protein kinase NIK (also called mitogen-activated protein 3 kinase 14 or MAP3K14) both in vitro and in vivo.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the epub (2013-12-22); no ibrutinib patient genotype-response data then.
efficacy.model: MCL cell-line pharmacogenomic panel (classical vs alternative NF-kB; TRAF2/BIRC3 lesions predict ibrutinib insensitivity)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). The BIRC3 effect is reported for the RAY cohort, not shown separately for the ibrutinib arm, so it may be prognostic rather than ibrutinib-specific.
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison of Rahal's cell-line prediction with BIRC3 outcomes in RAY (PFS primary). Freeman reports the BIRC3 effect for the whole cohort, including the temsirolimus arm, so it does not test ibrutinib insensitivity: untested, unsettled (checker adjudication). Jain 2021 (first-line, with rituximab) is supporting only.
efficacy.note: In RAY (ibrutinib vs temsirolimus, R/R MCL), BIRC3 lesions carried worse outcomes across both arms, so prognostic; not shown for ibrutinib alone, so unsettled.
efficacy.quote: We showed the negative impact of BIRC3 mutations/deletions on outcomes in this cohort and identified that deletion of chromosome 8p23.3 also negatively impacts survival.

patient_trials.quote: Differential overexpression of CCND1, BIRC3, BANK1, SETBP1, AXIN2, and IL2RA was noted in partial responders compared with patients with complete response.

efficacy.reason: BIRC3 effect pooled across RAY arms
efficacy.model: MCL cell-line pharmacogenomic panel (classical vs alternative NF-kB; TRAF2/BIRC3 lesions predict ibrutinib insensitivity)
Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the acalabrutinib track: the canine trial was first public 2016, after ibrutinib MCL responses (2011).
efficacy.note: Twenty pet dogs with B-cell lymphoma got acalabrutinib; 25% responded. Opening entry of the acalabrutinib track.
efficacy.quote: Overall response rate (ORR) was 25% (5/20) with a median progression free survival (PFS) of 22.5 days.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: objective response: 25% in dogs vs 81% in R/R MCL
efficacy.model: Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Lancet online 2017-12-11; NCT02213926 results posted 2018-10-19.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction by post-dating: the dog acalabrutinib result (2016) came after ibrutinib MCL responses were public (2011), so reproducing response is retro, not same. Dogs under-called magnitude again.
efficacy.note: Single-arm phase 2 ACE-LY-004, primary endpoint ORR, no pre-set success bar: 81% responded in R/R MCL; dogs responded too, but after BTK inhibition was known to work in MCL.
efficacy.quote: At a median follow-up of 15·2 months, 100 (81%) patients achieved an overall response and 49 (40%) patients achieved a complete response.
efficacy.reason: Dogs responded after MCL result known

safety.confidence_note: Year proxy: first-in-human trial posted 2009-02-24, so toxicology preceded it.
safety.model: GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology (rat, dog)
safety.note: Rat and dog toxicology named GI tract and lymphoid tissue as target organs; dog telemetry showed no QT effect. Unpublished before review.
safety.quote: The target organs of ibrutinib are GI tract and lymphoid tissues.

safety.magnitude_basis: platelet counts: rose in rats and dogs, fell in patients
safety.confidence_note: Review signed 2013 (Reference ID 3360071), posted under the 2014 NDA folder; year is the posting. The review's QT call held (no QTc prolongation in patients). The 2013 Orig1 copy of the pharmacology review is not posted on accessdata (404), so the earliest public copy is the 2014 Orig2 posting and year 2014 stands.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: thrombocytopenia in R/R MCL is partly disease-driven, but the regulator itself states the contrast and platelet counts moved the opposite way in animals. Atrial fibrillation (in the label from 2014) was also absent from dog telemetry; dogs can show it, so it supports the miss. QT silence matched and does not outweigh the miss.
safety.model: GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology (rat, dog)
safety.note: FDA reviewers noted animals showed raised, not lowered, platelets; patients had thrombocytopenia, bleeding and atrial fibrillation the toxicology did not flag.
safety.quote: Of note, one common adverse effect in patients treated with ibrutinib, thrombocytopenia, was not observed non-clinically.

safety.confidence_note: Proxy year: first-in-human BGB-3111-AU-003 started 2014-09-04; toxicology data unpublished until the 2019 review.
safety.note: Rat (26-week) and dog (39-week) toxicology and dog telemetry supported first-in-human dosing of zanubrutinib.
safety.quote: Zanubrutinib was administered once daily to rats and dogs in studies up to 6 months in rats and 9 months in dogs.
safety.model: Zanubrutinib GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology (rat, dog)

safety.confidence_note: Bundled review text (Reference ID 4519846); quote cleaned of OCR spacing. The review lists animal multi-organ hemorrhage, which matched patient bleeding; R/R MCL thrombocytopenia 28% from the review's adverse-event table.
safety.judgement: Judgement call, as on the ibrutinib track: hemorrhage was predicted and held, but platelets rose in the 39-week dog study while R/R MCL patients had thrombocytopenia (33/117, 28%); the miss on a harm dogs can show outweighs the matched bleeding. Atrial fibrillation/flutter is reported for the pooled B-cell population (none or about 1% in R/R MCL), so it does not count against the model for this tile.
safety.note: Animals showed bleeding, matching patient hemorrhage, but platelets rose in dogs while 28% of R/R MCL patients had thrombocytopenia. Atrial fibrillation (2%) is from the pooled B-cell safety set, not MCL, so not scored here.
safety.quote: The inflammatory response together with reduced erythrocytes, hemoglobin, hematocrit suggest bleeding in animals and may explain increased platelet levels.
safety.reason: Platelets rose in dogs, fell in MCL
safety.model: Zanubrutinib GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology (rat, dog)

safety.confidence_note: Proxy year: first-in-human ACE-CL-001 (NCT02029443) started 2014-01-30; toxicology unpublished until the 2017 review.
safety.note: Rat (26-week) and dog (91-day, 39-week) toxicology and dog telemetry supported first-in-human dosing of acalabrutinib.
safety.quote: Sprague-Dawley rats were administered doses up to 300 mg/kg in the 26-week study and Beagle dogs were administered doses up to 30 mg/kg in the 91-day (3-month) and 39-week studies.
safety.model: Acalabrutinib GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology (rat, dog)

safety.confidence_note: Bundled review text (Reference ID 4173186). Animals: dog red-cell decreases, no telemetry effect, rat heart hemorrhage only at lethal doses, no platelet finding. ACE-LY-004 (n=124): hemorrhage 31.5%, platelets decreased 44%, anemia, atrial fibrillation 0.
safety.judgement: Judgement call, as on the ibrutinib and zanubrutinib tracks: dog red-cell decreases matched anemia and telemetry silence matched no AF in the MCL pivotal trial, but tolerated-dose animals flagged neither the bleeding (31.5%) nor the platelet decreases (44%); the missed harms outweigh the matches.
safety.note: Dog telemetry and tolerated-dose toxicology showed no bleeding or platelet effect; MCL patients had frequent bleeding and platelet decreases, though no atrial fibrillation.
safety.quote: Following single oral doses, acalabrutinib had no toxicologically-significant effects on cardiovascular function in a cardiovascular study in telemetered dogs
safety.model: Acalabrutinib GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology (rat, dog)
Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
safety.judgement: Opening entry: the canine system existed (ASH 2009 abstract) before it made a tolerability statement.
safety.note: Pet dogs with B-cell lymphoma were dosed with ibrutinib before human data; their tolerability was reported in PNAS 2010.
safety.quote: PCI-32765 is an oral, potent and selective covalent inhibitor of Btk which blocks BCR signaling and inhibits tumor growth in both mouse and spontaneous canine NHL models.

safety.magnitude_basis: overall tolerability: dogs at well-tolerated doses vs no AE discontinuations in R/R MCL
safety.model: Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
safety.confidence_note: Congress abstract (ASH 2011, Blood 118:442), interim 39 patients; PNAS dog statement read in full text.
safety.judgement: Passing tolerability claim scored as a safety prediction. Retrodiction by post-dating: the dog claim (PNAS 2010) came after patients on the phase 1 were reported as well tolerated (ASH 2009). Specific harms (thrombocytopenia, bleeding) are scored on the toxicology tracks.
safety.note: Dogs were treated "at well-tolerated doses" (PNAS 2010); R/R MCL patients on PCYC-1104 also tolerated ibrutinib, none stopping for adverse events.
safety.short: Tolerated in dogs and MCL patients
safety.quote: Treatment has been well tolerated. No patients have discontinued treatment due to AEs.
safety.reason: Tolerability matched after it was known

safety.model: Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the acalabrutinib track; the tolerability claim is in the same abstract.
safety.note: Dogs with B-cell lymphoma tolerated acalabrutinib with mostly grade 1-2 GI adverse events; a passing tolerability claim.
safety.quote: Acalabrutinib was generally well tolerated, with adverse events consisting primarily of grade 1 or 2 anorexia, weight loss, vomiting, diarrhea and lethargy.

safety.magnitude_basis: overall tolerability: mostly grade 1-2 AEs in dogs and in R/R MCL (6% stopped for AEs)
safety.model: Pet dogs with spontaneous B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Bleeding (31.5%) and platelet decreases are scored on the acalabrutinib toxicology track.
safety.judgement: Passing tolerability claim scored as a safety prediction. Retrodiction by post-dating on the drug's own result: the dog claim (July 2016) followed acalabrutinib's own phase 1-2 patient tolerability in CLL (Byrd, NEJM, December 2015). Ibrutinib's earlier MCL tolerability does not count for this dose/safety question.
safety.note: Dogs predicted acalabrutinib would be well tolerated; in ACE-LY-004 adverse events were mostly grade 1-2 and 6% of R/R MCL patients stopped for them. Retro because acalabrutinib's own CLL tolerability was public first.
safety.quote: Acalabrutinib treatment provided a high rate of durable responses and a favourable safety profile in patients with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma.
safety.reason: Tolerability matched after it was known
